scenario_name: Train Derailment & Chemical Tanker Rupture (214 Casualties, 5 Disruption Events)
disclaimer: CRITICAL NOTICE: All metrics represent simulated algorithmic and logistical throughput within a deterministic mathematical model. No real-world medical outcomes, clinical survival rates, or physiological end-points are claimed or evaluated.

baseline_profile.planning_methodology: Greedy Nearest-Hospital / Uncoordinated Radio Dispatch (No Global MILP Model)

lifelink_profile.planning_methodology: Constrained OR-Tools MILP Solver & Multi-Agent Continuous Replanning Loop

metrics_comparison.operational_meaning: Initial incident dispatch plan generated in milliseconds vs multi-channel radio coordination delay.

metrics_comparison.metric_name: Critical Patients Assigned to Feasible Care
metrics_comparison.operational_meaning: Systematic allocation of all critical casualties to facilities with verified clinical capabilities.
Zero critical casualties lost in transit or field queues; all deficits linked to mutual aid alarms.
Eliminates secondary inter-facility transports by enforcing zero-tolerance bed constraints.
Maximizes vehicle productivity by avoiding severed highway corridors and facility turnaways.
Simultaneously optimizes across blood units, ventilators, trauma teams, and USAR squads.
Continuously updates assignments whenever hospital beds, roads, or casualty censuses change.
Automated algorithmic re-planning takes milliseconds compared to manual phone tree coordination.

executive_summary: SIMULATION BENCHMARK SUMMARY: In a simulated 214-casualty mass disruption event, LIFELINK's OR-Tools MILP optimization generated feasible initial crisis assignments in 41.1 ms (vs 14.5 min manual baseline), completely eliminated hospital ICU diversion conflicts (0 vs 4), increased ambulance utilization from 52.4% to 96.2%, and executed 5 continuous automated replans with an average latency of 34.7 ms per event.
